title: Norway Proposes Temporary Ban on AI Smart Glasses in Public
subtitle: New government plans aim to address growing privacy concerns as wearable camera technology becomes more common.

summary.en: Norway is planning a temporary ban on AI smart glasses in many public spaces. The government wants to protect people from being recorded without their knowledge. This move follows similar restrictions in private businesses like cinemas and restaurants. Meta, the maker of popular smart glasses, says its devices have safety lights to show when they are recording. The government will now study the issue to decide on permanent rules.
summary.zh: 挪威計畫在許多公共場所暫時禁止使用人工智慧智慧眼鏡。政府希望保護民眾免於在不知情的情況下被錄影。此舉跟進了電影院和餐廳等私人企業類似的限制措施。熱門智慧眼鏡製造商 Meta 表示，其裝置配有安全指示燈，可顯示錄影狀態。挪威政府將進一步研究此議題，以決定永久性的規範。

paragraphs.en: Norway has taken a bold step in the world of technology by proposing a temporary ban on AI-enabled smart glasses in various public places. This decision makes Norway the first major country to attempt a national restriction on these wearable devices. The government plans to introduce a bill to parliament that would stop people from using camera-equipped glasses in areas such as parks, beaches, schools, museums, and gyms.
paragraphs.zh: 挪威在科技領域邁出了大膽的一步，提議在多個公共場所暫時禁止使用具備人工智慧功能的智慧眼鏡。這項決定使挪威成為第一個嘗試對此類穿戴式裝置實施全國性限制的主要國家。政府計畫向國會提交法案，禁止民眾在公園、海灘、學校、博物館和健身房等區域使用配備攝影鏡頭的眼鏡。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian World, the government is worried about the rapid spread of technology that allows users to record others without permission. Torgeir Micaelsen, Norway’s minister of digital affairs, explained that he is concerned about a society where people feel they are being watched or recorded in places where they usually expect privacy. He noted that the temporary ban is intended to give officials time to study the issue carefully and create permanent rules for the future.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報》(The Guardian) 報導，挪威政府對於允許使用者在未經許可下錄製他人的技術迅速擴散感到憂心。挪威數位事務部長米凱爾森 (Torgeir Micaelsen) 解釋，他擔憂社會大眾在通常預期享有隱私的地方，會感到自己正受到監視或錄影。他指出，這項臨時禁令旨在讓官員有時間審慎研究此議題，並為未來制定永久性的規範。

paragraphs.en: This new proposal is part of a growing trend of restrictions on smart glasses. As Ars Technica reports, some parts of Norwegian society have already acted on their own. For example, schools in Oslo and the large company Equinor have already banned the devices from their offices and facilities. These local actions reflect a wider global concern about privacy. In the United Kingdom, many restaurants and cinemas have already introduced their own policies to restrict or ban the glasses. These businesses are worried about both the privacy of their customers and the illegal recording of films.
paragraphs.zh: 這項新提案是智慧眼鏡限制趨勢日益增長的一部分。正如科技新聞網站《Ars Technica》報導，挪威社會的部分群體已經採取了自主行動。例如，奧斯陸的學校以及大型能源公司挪威國家石油公司 (Equinor) 已禁止在辦公室和設施內使用這些裝置。這些地方性的行動反映了全球對隱私問題的廣泛關注。在英國，許多餐廳和電影院也已實施各自的政策來限制或禁止使用這類眼鏡。這些業者不僅擔心顧客的隱私，也憂慮電影遭到非法錄製。

paragraphs.en: At the center of this debate are devices like the smart glasses sold by Meta, the company that owns Facebook. These glasses allow users to take photos, record videos, make phone calls, and use AI tools. Since the start of 2023, Meta has sold at least 9 million pairs of its Ray-Ban smart glasses. While these products are popular, they have also caused problems. In France, a child welfare group called E-enfance reported receiving around 20 cases this year where women were filmed without their knowledge. Many of these videos were later posted on social media as pranks or interviews.
paragraphs.zh: 這場辯論的核心是諸如 Meta（擁有臉書的母公司）所販售的智慧眼鏡等裝置。這些眼鏡允許使用者拍照、錄影、撥打電話以及使用人工智慧工具。自 2023 年初以來，Meta 已售出至少 900 萬副雷朋 (Ray-Ban) 智慧眼鏡。儘管這些產品很受歡迎，但也引發了問題。在法國，一個名為「童年」(E-enfance) 的兒童福利組織報告稱，今年接獲約 20 起女性在不知情下被拍攝的案件。許多這類影片後來被當作惡作劇或採訪內容發布在社群媒體上。

paragraphs.en: Meta has defended its products by highlighting the safety features built into the glasses. A spokesperson for the company explained that every pair of glasses with a camera has a bright LED light on the front. This light blinks when the user is taking a photo or recording a video. The company states that this light cannot be turned off and that the camera will stop working if someone tries to cover or break it. Meta also advises its users to be respectful and stop recording if someone asks them to stop.
paragraphs.zh: Meta 為其產品辯護，強調眼鏡內建的安全功能。該公司發言人解釋，每一副配備攝影鏡頭的眼鏡前方都有一個明亮的發光二極體 (LED) 指示燈。當使用者拍照或錄影時，此燈會閃爍。公司聲明該燈無法關閉，且若有人試圖遮蓋或破壞它，攝影鏡頭將停止運作。Meta 也建議使用者應保持尊重，若有人要求停止錄影，應配合停止。

paragraphs.en: However, not everyone is convinced that these lights are enough. While some governments are moving toward stricter rules, others are taking a different approach. In the United States, for example, the governor of California, Gavin Newsom, recently vetoed a bill that would have punished people for using smart glasses to record others in private spaces like changing rooms or doctors’ offices. The governor noted that California already has laws in place to deal with illegal recording, suggesting that new legislation was not necessary.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，並非所有人都認為這些指示燈已足夠。當一些政府正朝向更嚴格的規範邁進時，其他政府則採取了不同的做法。例如在美國，加州州長紐森 (Gavin Newsom) 最近否決了一項法案，該法案原定懲罰在更衣室或醫生診間等私人空間使用智慧眼鏡錄製他人的行為。州長指出，加州現已有法律處理非法錄影，認為沒有必要制定新法。

paragraphs.en: As the debate continues, the Norwegian government is moving forward with its plan. The Labour party, which leads the country, needs support from other political parties to pass the bill. They hope to submit the proposal as soon as possible while also forming an expert group to look at the long-term impact of AI wearables. For now, the world is watching to see if other countries will follow Norway’s lead in regulating this powerful new technology. The goal for many officials is to find a balance between allowing people to enjoy new gadgets and protecting the basic right to privacy in public life.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著辯論持續進行，挪威政府正推進其計畫。執政的工黨需要其他政黨的支持才能通過法案。他們希望儘快提交提案，同時組成專家小組研究人工智慧穿戴式裝置的長期影響。目前，全世界都在關注是否有其他國家會跟隨挪威的腳步，對這項強大的新技術進行監管。對許多官員而言，目標是在讓民眾享受新科技產品與保護公共生活中基本的隱私權之間，找到平衡點。

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第一段，挪威政府計畫禁止在公園、海灘、學校、博物館和健身房（gyms）使用這類裝置。選項 A 並未提及，選項 C 和 D 雖為公共場所但文章中並未明確列出，屬於干擾選項。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, why might the Norwegian government's proposed ban be considered a 'temporary' measure?

options.A: Because the government expects the technology to become obsolete within a few years.
options.B: Because they are waiting for Meta to voluntarily stop selling the glasses.
options.C: Because officials need time to study the issue to develop more permanent, long-term regulations.
options.D: Because they only want to test if the public will follow the rules before making them permanent.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第二段，挪威數位事務部長指出，實施暫時性禁令是為了讓官員有時間仔細研究此議題，並為未來制定永久性的規範。選項 A、B、D 皆無法從文中推論得出，特別是政府並非等待 Meta 自行停售，而是主動介入立法。

quiz.question: In the context of the sixth paragraph, what does the word 'vetoed' mean?
quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在第六段中，提到加州州長 Gavin Newsom 對一項法案進行了 vetoed，隨後文中提到他認為不需要新立法，這顯示他拒絕或否決了該法案。選項 A 與 vetoed 意思相反；選項 C 和 D 與否決法案的語境不符。
